requested.title: Shell expansion bypasses all protected Git-command checks

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The current guard explicitly performs textual tokenization rather than shell parsing, and its header acknowledges that `g=git; $g reset --hard` passes. `splitSegments` analyzes `g=git` and `$g <subcommand>` independently, while `gitInvocation()` only recognizes a literal `git` token or a path ending in `/git`; `$g` therefore returns null. In the actual shell, the assignment persists across the semicolon and `$g` expands to `git`, so commands such as `g=git; $g push`, `g=git; $g reset --hard`, and `g=git; $g config core.hooksPath .ci/hooks` execute after approval. OpenCode configures `bash` as `ask`, but `decidePermission()` grants every command for which `checkCommand()` returns allowed, and the supervisor sends that approval to OpenCode without an additional Git-aware enforcement layer. The local execution path passes the same guard with `{ local: true }`; it intentionally permits local commits but still relies on this guard to prohibit pushes and dangerous config changes. A repository/task prompt injection can direct the agent to run the variable-indirected command, create a hook directory outside `.git`, and set `core.hooksPath`, producing persistent code execution on a later user Git action; it can also bypass the `create_pr` delivery gate with a direct push when the user's configured Git credentials are usable. Recent MIN-360 changes added literal checks for Git configuration, `.git` paths, wrappers, and shell `-c` payloads, but did not address expansion and retain the documented bypass. No framework-level protection observed in the permission pipeline resolves or rejects shell expansion before execution.
